summary: # Marvelous Designer Official Tutorial Video: Furniture Production P04 - Making a Small Quilt ## Introduction In this tutorial, we will create a small quilt using Marvelous Designer. We will cover various techniques, including simulation settings, fabric adjustments, and panel arrangement to achieve a realistic quilt design. ## Setting Up the Board Build a **500mm x 900mm board** to make a small quilt. Rotate the quilt and let it be simulated on the ground. ## Creating the Inflow Effect 1. Cut a layer to create the inflow effect. 2. Turn the surface over and let the front face all the way out. 3. Select the two front and back panels. 4. Apply pressure on the front and back panels. Set the pressure to **3** to enhance the inflow effect. ### Adjusting Pressure If the inflow is slower, you can remove some panels manually to make the inflow more visible. Since we are making the quilt inside, the pressure of **3** may be too obvious; therefore, reduce it to **2**. ## Customizing Fabric Lines Change the shape of the fabric line to **Custom Angle**. We need to make the curves smoother on the sides. 1. Cut a layer to ensure the plate of the quilter fits on the outside of the original plate. 2. Save some steps by removing the joint of the newly created board and deleting the sewing line. ### Sewing Adjustments Because the board has been turned over on the surface, if the sewing line is not certain, you can separate the two boards and sew them with the sewing tool in the **3D window**. ## Simulation and Layer Management Turn on the simulation. When the outer layer is smaller than the inner layer, the outer layer will deform, allowing it to be placed on the outer layer. ### Resolving Deformation Issues When there are two layers of boards, greater deformation may occur if the wire gap cannot penetrate. Return to the starting point: the outer layer should be slightly narrower. ## Center Point Adjustments The center point of the double machine frame can activate the center point function. The following adjustments will be based on the center point. More detailed explanations will follow. ### Back Cover Pressure Adjustment The outer layer of the back cover has been molded before, retaining the pressure of the original version. Adjust the pressure of the outer layer to **0**, as the back cover is usually single-layer and has no inflow. If the back cover is pressed due to the pressure of the outer version, you can increase the pressure to **3**. ## Applying New Fabric 1. Add a new fabric and drag it to the selected panel. 2. Apply the new fabric to the small quilt panel. 3. Change the fabric to **silk taffeta**, a synthetic fabric that is easy to work with. 4. Reduce the density of this fabric to lighten the weight of the panel and enhance the fluffy feel of the quilt. ### Copying Inner Fabric Copy the inner fabric and increase the friction coefficient. This ensures that random creases made during subsequent manual fabric dragging do not dissipate due to fabric sliding. ## Enhancing Visual Appeal Close the mat to make the desktop look more magnificent. Now we can place the curtain under the cover and attach the most important part of the **pápi**. ### Placing the Curtain 1. Lay the curtain on the back of the quilt at an angle of **1.5 inches** and push the pattern to the front from both sides. 2. Place the curtain on the top of the pillow and press it to the top. 3. You can also place the curtain over the block of the quilt and press it to the back of the pillow to enhance the pattern's visibility. ## Simulation Speed Adjustment If the simulation speed is slow, press the simulation button to switch to **GPU simulation**. Reduce the example time to **8** to make it more detailed. ### Final Adjustments After adjusting to the right position, press the **W key** to click on the tabletop. You can click on the tabletop again and add a fixed needle to the position of the tabletop to secure the small cup. ## Maintaining the Fold Effect After removing the cup, pause the simulation and add a needle to maintain the effect of the fold before it disappears. The basic adjustment is that the friction coefficient of the surface should be relatively high. ### Stability of the Fold If the friction coefficient is not high, the fold will soon disappear, and stability will be compromised. The fold will be more stable with a higher friction coefficient. ## Finalizing the Simulation Press the **W key** to click on the fixed needle again to delete it. Thanks for watching! ### Additional Steps Add some fixed creases to the position needle. After the simulation is stable, return to the default simulation tool and simulate again. After that, select these panels and delete the fixed creases on the panels in the menu on the right. When the simulation has stopped, you can continue with the simulation.
